COMMITTEE ON SANITATION & SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT 85 One of the main supporting arguments for implementing a wheeled container system was the ease with which it could be utilized with the current fleet of trucks. The report mentioned that this could be realized with retrofitting. Can you please explain what retrofitting would be necessary?

Yeah. For the large buildings, the buildings of 31 units or more, there are two options to containerize trash. They both involve large four-cubic-yard containers. The options are four-cubic-yard containers on wheels or fourcubic-yard containers not on wheels. We piloted the four-cubic-yard containers on wheels because you can roll that container up to the back of a normal sanitation truck that's slightly retrofitted with a tipper, put that big container on a tipper and tip it into the back of the truck. That's not the go-forward strategy for New York City because I think having hundreds of thousands of four-cubic-yard containers on wheels in this city is a terrible idea for safety reasons, for many reasons, so the go-forward model involves the four-cubic-yard containers not having wheels, and instead of using the retrofitted truck, we would use a special side-loading truck that we
